title: Quantum speed limits based on quantifiers of quantum-state texture
authors: Yuhang Xie, Yanjun Chu, Chenyang Cui, Shao-Ming Fei
abstract: Quantum speed limits impose intrinsic lower bounds on the shortest time scale for quantum system evolution. As an emerging paradigm in quantum resource theory, quantum-state texture has attracted research interest amid the rapid advancement of quantum theory. Herein, we investigate the interplay between quantum speed limits and quantum-state texture via several canonical quantifiers, including trace distance, state rugosity and Jensen-Shannon divergence. To demonstrate our findings, we analyze the minimum evolution time of physical systems subject to dephasing and dissipative dynamics. For the Jensen-Shannon divergence, we further explore nonunitary dynamics described by completely positive and trace-preserving maps, taking the amplitude damping channel as a typical example. In addition, we explore the tightness of these bounds in the considered dynamical models. Our results reveal that quantum speed limits derived from quantum-state texture capture the fundamental constraints on quantum evolutionary speed, with promising applications in quantum computing, quantum control and quantum metrology.
summary: This paper establishes a theoretical link between Quantum Speed Limits and Quantum-State Texture, using measures like trace distance and Jensen-Shannon divergence. By analyzing specific open quantum systems, the authors derive quantitative lower bounds on the minimum evolution time. This framework offers new diagnostic tools for understanding fundamental constraints in quantum control and metrology.
main_problem: The paper investigates the fundamental lower bounds on the time scale of quantum evolution (Quantum Speed Limits, QSLs) by linking them to the quantitative measure of quantum-state texture (QST).
main_result: QSLs derived from various QST quantifiers, such as trace distance, state rugosity, and Jensen-Shannon divergence, successfully capture the fundamental constraints on quantum evolutionary speed.
method: The authors derive lower bounds ($	au \ge 	au_{QSL}$) by analyzing the time evolution of the chosen QST measure using various mathematical tools, including analyzing the time derivative of the measure.
model_or_system: The analysis considers general quantum systems undergoing evolution, specifically modeling dephasing and dissipative dynamics using master equations. Examples include a two-level atom coupled to a bosonic reservoir or analyzed via the amplitude damping channel.
key_observables: Quantum Speed Limits ($	au_{QSL}$), Trace Distance ($\Delta_{	ext{tr}}$), State Rugosity ($\Delta R$), Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD), and the normalized relative error ($	ilde{\delta}$).
important_parameters: Dephasing rate ($\gamma_t$), cavity decay rate ($\gamma_t$), and initial state parameters ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis involves approximations for non-unitary dynamics (CPTP maps) and relies on defining the QSL based on the rate of change of the QST measure.
figures_summary: The notes mention numerical observations showing the behavior of $	au_{QSL}^{JS}$ and the relative error $	ilde{\delta}_{JS}(	au)$ for different parameter regimes, indicating when the bound is tight or loose.
paper_structure: The paper systematically introduces QSLs and QST, derives bounds using different quantifiers (trace distance, rugosity, JSD), and applies these derivations to specific physical models like dephasing and amplitude damping channels.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides a generalized framework for deriving fundamental time constraints in open quantum systems, connecting resource theory concepts (QST) directly to fundamental physical limits (QSLs).
